title: Multi-Site Inverter and Battery Backup for CIHP
summary: Integrated Solutions Technology delivered inverter and battery backup installations for four CIHP facilities in Abuja, Falomo, LASUTH and Idah, using different equipment configurations for the participating sites.
challenge:
A multi-location energy project needs to account for each facility rather than assume one equipment package suits every site. CIHP's recorded scope covered facilities in Abuja, Lagos and Kogi State, with a different inverter and battery arrangement in Abuja from the three other installations.

The requirement was to provide inverter and stored-energy infrastructure across these separate locations. The supplied records describe the installed equipment, but do not include facility load schedules, measured outages or required backup duration.
solutionNarrative: The Abuja installation used a 10 kW, 48 V system with lithium storage. The storage entry is written as ‘15KW Lithium’ in the installation register, so an energy capacity in kWh cannot be confirmed from that entry.

At Falomo, LASUTH and Zonal Hospital in Idah, the recorded configuration was a 5 kVA hybrid inverter with twelve 200 Ah wet-cell batteries at each facility. Presenting the sites separately preserves the distinction between the lithium installation and the wet-cell battery installations.
solution: Abuja: 10 kW, 48 V inverter system with lithium storage.
Falomo, Lagos: 5 kVA hybrid inverter and 12 × 200 Ah wet-cell batteries.
LASUTH, Lagos: 5 kVA hybrid inverter and 12 × 200 Ah wet-cell batteries.
Zonal Hospital, Idah: 5 kVA hybrid inverter and 12 × 200 Ah wet-cell batteries.
result:
The delivered scope provided inverter and battery backup equipment at four institutional facilities across three geographical areas. It demonstrates experience coordinating energy installations across separate healthcare and institutional environments.

Solar panel quantities and measured backup performance are not included in these records. This project is therefore described as inverter and battery backup delivery, without claiming a recorded PV installation or a verified runtime.

specifications.battery: Lithium storage; capacity unit to be confirmed

evidenceNote: The Abuja battery is recorded as ‘15KW Lithium’. This has not been converted into a kWh claim. Installation dates and measured runtime were not supplied.

faqs.question: Which CIHP facilities received inverter and battery installations?
faqs.answer: The project records list CIHP Abuja, CIHP Falomo in Lagos, CIHP LASUTH in Lagos and CIHP Zonal Hospital in Idah, Kogi State.

faqs.question: Did every CIHP site use the same battery configuration?
faqs.answer: No. Abuja is recorded with lithium storage. Falomo, LASUTH and Idah each have twelve 200 Ah wet-cell batteries alongside a 5 kVA hybrid inverter.

faqs.question: How long do these backup systems run?
faqs.answer: The records do not state measured runtime. Backup duration depends on the connected load, usable battery energy, battery condition and system settings; inverter ratings and battery amp-hours alone do not establish it.

title: Separate Backup Power Systems for PiggyTech’s Server Room and Office
summary: Two PiggyTech installations in Victoria Island paired a 10 kVA inverter with 15 kWh lithium storage for the server room and a 12 kVA MUST inverter with two 15 kWh batteries for the office.
challenge:
A server room and a general office serve different activities and can require different power arrangements. PiggyTech's project covered these environments as two separate installations, rather than treating the premises as one undifferentiated load.

The recorded requirement was to provide inverter and lithium battery equipment for the server room in October 2026 and for the office in November 2026. The source does not specify equipment loads, a guaranteed autonomy period or measured service availability.
solutionNarrative: The server-room installation combined a 10 kVA inverter with 15 kWh of lithium battery storage. This provided a dedicated inverter-and-storage configuration for that part of the business.

The office installation used a 12 kVA MUST inverter and two 15 kWh lithium batteries. Those battery nameplate capacities total 30 kWh. Keeping the two installations distinct makes the delivered capacity in each environment clear without suggesting that their inverters form a single combined system.
solution: Server room: 10 kVA inverter and 15 kWh lithium battery storage.
Office: 12 kVA MUST inverter and 2 × 15 kWh lithium batteries.
result:
PiggyTech received two separately specified inverter and lithium storage installations for its server room and office. The office battery configuration has a larger recorded nameplate energy capacity than the server-room configuration, reflecting the distinct equipment selections.

This is a documented backup-power project. Although the source document groups it with solar projects, neither the case-study scope nor the installation register lists solar panels for these two installations. No PV capacity, verified uptime improvement or operating-cost reduction is claimed.

faqs.question: What backup power equipment was installed for PiggyTech?
faqs.answer: The server room received a 10 kVA inverter with 15 kWh lithium storage. The office received a 12 kVA MUST inverter with two 15 kWh lithium batteries.

faqs.question: Does 30 kWh of battery storage mean 30 hours of backup?
faqs.answer: No. kWh measures stored energy, not a fixed number of hours. Actual backup duration depends on the connected load, usable battery capacity, conversion losses and operating settings.

faqs.question: Were solar panels included in this installation?
faqs.answer: Solar panels are not listed in the supplied PiggyTech records. The documented scope is inverter and lithium battery backup for the server room and office.

title: Two Solar Systems for Ernneka’s Shop and Office in Lagos
summary: Integrated Solutions Technology installed separate solar systems for Ernneka’s shop and office, combining hybrid inverters, 15 kWh lithium batteries and Jinko solar panels in two different configurations.
challenge:
Ernneka's shop and office needed separate solar installations. The two premises were not specified with identical equipment: the shop had a larger inverter rating and a different panel array from the office.

The requirement was to bring solar generation, inverter conversion and battery storage together at both premises while preserving each installation's individual configuration. The project record supplies equipment quantities, but not load-assessment results or a measured energy baseline.
solutionNarrative: The shop installation paired a 12 kVA hybrid inverter with a 15 kWh lithium battery and sixteen 590 W Jinko panels. The panels have a combined nameplate rating of 9.44 kWp, calculated as 16 × 590 W.

The office installation used a 10 kVA hybrid inverter, a 15 kWh lithium battery and eight 715 W Jinko panels. This array has a calculated nameplate rating of 5.72 kWp. Both systems included the same recorded battery energy capacity, while their inverter ratings and panel configurations differed.
solution: Shop: 12 kVA hybrid inverter, 15 kWh lithium battery and 16 × 590 W Jinko panels.
Office: 10 kVA hybrid inverter, 15 kWh lithium battery and 8 × 715 W Jinko panels.
result:
The completed scope provided two commercial premises with solar generation, hybrid inverter equipment and lithium storage. It shows how separate business locations can use different combinations of panels and inverter capacity rather than a single standard package.

The panel ratings describe installed nameplate capacity. They are not a prediction of daily energy generation, and the records do not quantify fuel savings, electricity savings or backup duration.

faqs.question: What solar capacity was installed at Ernneka’s shop and office?
faqs.answer: The shop has sixteen 590 W panels, totalling 9.44 kWp. The office has eight 715 W panels, totalling 5.72 kWp. These figures are calculated from the recorded panel quantities and ratings.

faqs.question: Did the shop and office use identical solar systems?
faqs.answer: No. The shop used a 12 kVA hybrid inverter and the office used a 10 kVA hybrid inverter. Each had a 15 kWh lithium battery, with a different panel configuration.

faqs.question: What does this project show about commercial solar design?
faqs.answer: It documents two premises using distinct inverter and solar-array configurations. A new commercial installation should be assessed against its own loads, available space and backup requirements.

The recorded combination needed to be presented as a single installation while keeping the three different ratings clear: inverter capacity in kVA, battery energy in kWh and panel nameplate power in watts.
solutionNarrative: Integrated Solutions Technology delivered a 10 kVA hybrid inverter with 16 kWh of lithium battery storage and twelve 620 W Jinko solar panels. The recorded panels total 7.44 kWp of nameplate capacity, calculated as 12 × 620 W.

The hybrid inverter, battery and PV array form the documented equipment scope. The installation record does not specify an appliance schedule, daily energy yield or a guaranteed overnight backup duration.

16 kWh lithium battery storage.

result:

title: Two Residential Solar Configurations at Sunshine Estate
summary: Two Sunshine Estate installations used different configurations: a 3 kVA, 24 V hybrid inverter with six panels and a 6 kVA, 48 V hybrid inverter with 10 kWh lithium storage and four panels.
challenge:
Homes within one estate do not necessarily require identical energy systems. The Sunshine Estate records document two residential installations with different inverter ratings, DC system voltages and panel quantities.

The project requirement was to deliver these as individual installations. The records do not include a load comparison between the households, so the equipment differences should not be interpreted as a measured comparison of their electricity consumption.
solutionNarrative: In July 2025, the recorded installation was a 3 kVA, 24 V hybrid inverter with six 625 W Jinko panels. Those panels total 3.75 kWp. No battery specification is listed for this installation.
In November 2025, a separate installation used a 6 kVA, 48 V hybrid inverter with 10 kWh of lithium storage and four 625 W Jinko panels. The recorded PV nameplate rating for this system is 2.50 kWp.
solution: July 2025: 3 kVA, 24 V hybrid inverter and 6 × 625 W Jinko panels.
November 2025: 6 kVA, 48 V hybrid inverter, 10 kWh lithium storage and 4 × 625 W Jinko panels.
result:
Two residential installations were delivered at Sunshine Estate with distinct equipment combinations. The project illustrates that a larger inverter rating does not automatically imply a larger installed solar array: the November system had the larger inverter, while the July system had more recorded panels.

Battery capacity is confirmed only for the November installation. The missing July battery entry is left unspecified rather than filled with an assumed value.

faqs.question: How many installations are recorded for Sunshine Estate?
faqs.answer: Two separate residential solar installations are recorded, one in July 2025 and one in November 2025.

faqs.question: What battery was used in the November installation?
faqs.answer: The November 2025 record specifies a 10 kWh lithium battery with a 6 kVA, 48 V hybrid inverter. The July record does not specify battery capacity.

faqs.question: Why does the larger inverter system have fewer panels?
faqs.answer: Inverter capacity and PV array size describe different aspects of a system. The records confirm different equipment configurations but do not state the design reasoning or load assessment for either household.

solutionNarrative: General Hospital Kawo is recorded with a 5 kVA hybrid inverter and twelve 200 Ah wet-cell batteries. General Hospital Zaria has the same recorded inverter and battery configuration.

The battery amp-hour rating and quantity are retained as supplied. Battery voltage and the bank's series/parallel configuration are not listed, so a total stored-energy figure in kWh cannot be calculated reliably from these entries.
solution: General Hospital Kawo: 5 kVA hybrid inverter and 12 × 200 Ah wet-cell batteries.
General Hospital Zaria: 5 kVA hybrid inverter and 12 × 200 Ah wet-cell batteries.
result:
